title: EU financial services evidence delivery and segmentation checklist 2026
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This checklist captures the operator-level technical artifacts and validation steps required to satisfy baseline EU financial services evidence requests for Redwood Private deployments. It covers network segmentation proof, key management and HSM boundary evidence, telemetry and audit bundles, KV cache snapshot handling for upgrades/rollbacks, and the operator's evidence delivery process. Use this as the operator baseline; customers may add stricter contractual controls.

Audience
- Delivery engineers, security evidence custodians, deployment engineering leads, and customer security reviewers.

Principles
- Minimize sensitive exposure: redact or mask customer PII in audit exports prior to delivery.
- Tamper-evidence: every evidence bundle must include a manifest and an operator signature.
- Traceability: map each artifact to an acceptance test and sign-off.

Required artifacts (per delivery)
- Manifest file: canonical list of artifacts, creator, timestamp, and checksums.
- Network segmentation export: deployed subnet CIDRs, security group rules, and egress ACLs.
- KMS/HSM evidence: key metadata, rotation timestamps, operator role bindings, and HSM attestation where applicable.
- Telemetry and audit bundle: sampled traces, operator API audit lines, model swap records, and a traceID mapping file.
- KV cache snapshot: compressed snapshot with checksum and a manifest entry noting provenance.
- Image provenance: image digests, SBOM summaries, and signature indicators.

Acceptance tests (operator-run)
1) Tenant isolation test- Attempt cross-tenant connectivity probes from a controlled probe host; expect failure. Run three probes from three different subnets. Record packet capture snippets showing drops or rejects.

2) Egress allowlist test- Verify tenant egress destinations limited to approved proxies and external services. Perform three allowed egress tests and capture DNS and flow logs.

3) KMS envelope test- Use an envelope encrypt/decrypt roundtrip with a transient test secret to prove CMK accessibility without leaking plaintext keys. Document timestamps and outcomes.

4) KV snapshot dry run- Load the snapshot into an isolated validation runtime and run a short smoke workload to confirm state restores and latency SLOs hold (p50 and p95 compared to baseline).

Evidence bundle composition and retention- The operator must produce a single archive per delivery that contains:
- MANIFEST.TXT: plain text manifest listing artifacts and checksums.
- artifacts/: network export, telemetry bundle, kv snapshot file, image provenance summary.
- signatures/: operator signature file and public key material.

Retention baseline (contractual minimum)
- Raw telemetry: 90 days.
- Signed manifests and summaries: 3 years.
- KV snapshots: 6 months unless customer specifies a longer retention.

Handover playbook (step-by-step)
1) Pre-handover (operator)- Produce artifacts, verify checksums, and sign the manifest. Run tenant isolation and KMS tests and collect logs.
2) Joint verification session- Schedule a 2 hour session with customer security contact. Present the manifest, walk through artifact locations, and demonstrate the tenant isolation and envelope tests.
3) Spot-test support- Support up to three customer spot-tests within the joint session. Provide trace payloads and a sealed validation runtime for safe replay.
4) Acceptance and exceptions- If all tests pass, customer signs acceptance. For any failed test, create a corrective action plan with severity and remediation timelines. High severity remediation <= 72 hours.

Upgrade and rollback evidence requirements- Before a major upgrade: capture pre-upgrade KV snapshot, pre-upgrade telemetry sample, and pre-upgrade image signatures. After the upgrade: capture post-upgrade KV snapshot, run a 1k token smoke suite, and collect latency percentiles p50, p95, p99.

On rollback: produce a rollback incident bundle that includes the trigger reason, rollback commands executed, artifacts restored, and post-rollback verification results. The rollback bundle must be signed and archived within 24 hours of the rollback.

Automation examples (operator commands)
- Create manifest: run the packaging tool to produce a manifest and checksum; sign using the operator signing key.
- Produce KV snapshot: use the runtime kv snapshot binary to emit a compressed snapshot and checksum.
- Collect telemetry: use the telemetry collector with a 24 hour window to produce an audit bundle.

Checklist for operator sign-off (mark PASS/FAIL)
- Manifest produced and signed.
- Network segmentation export present and matches deployed state.
- KMS/HSM rotation evidence included.
- Telemetry bundle contains referenced traceIDs.
- KV snapshot checksum verifies and dry-run restore succeeds.
- Image provenance present and signatures indicated.
- Bundle archived in immutable storage and access model documented.

Exceptions and mitigations
- Customer cannot host a CMK: document the exception in the manifest, implement a time-bound operator double-envelope process, and obtain customer sign-off.
- Airgapped site cannot verify signatures online: include signed artifact signatures and an offline verification tool in the bundle.

Contacts and escalation
- Evidence custodian: security-evidence at redwood dot ai (primary contact).
- Deployment engineering lead: liam dot patel at redwood dot ai.
- Escalation: deployment engineering lead -> Head of Private Deployments -> Legal.

Change history
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft by Maya Chen.
- 2026-02-25: Clarified KV snapshot dry-run acceptance and handover steps (reviewers: Liam Patel, Sofia Rodriguez).

Related templates
- Evidence bundle template located in the templates folder of the customer requirements library.
- Operator offline verification scripts for on-prem packaging available in the onprem packaging wiki.

Notes
- This checklist is a technical baseline only and does not substitute for contractual or legal requirements. Operators must escalate when a customer requests controls outside the scope of this document.
